name: Arcadian Green
lede: Arcadian Green is a pale, soft green from the color card of the 1920s.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Paterson defines arcadian green as a pale yellow-tinged green [1]. The library records it in Maerz and Paul's dictionary, first recorded in 1928, on plate 17 G 8 [2]. That is a fashion and textile source, and the name belongs to that world [2].

The books we hold define the color but never say why it was called Arcadian [1]. Its nearest named color is [[pistachio]], at a distance of 5.2 [2]. It sits in the family of pale greens that includes [[apple-green]] and [[celadon]] [2]. Paterson's index files it with the greens [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings it appears in 0.05% of the paintings, 11 of them, as photographed [3]. The earliest match is dated 1795, which is 133 years before the name's first record, so the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof of the pigment or dye [2][3].

notes.cite: Paterson, A Dictionary of Colour, p. 32, "arcadian green"

questions.q: A painting from 1795 that matches Arcadian Green proves the pigment existed then.
Where did Arcadian Green first appear in our library records?

openers: Arcadian Green was first recorded in 1928, in a color dictionary used by textile trades.
